admission.justification: The factory, pytest setup and explicit subprocess integrations share the selector cap, and an injected EPERM control prevents reintroducing a fixture hang that ordinary successful socket sends conceal.

applicability: Test-owned asyncio selector loops created by the shared factory for pytest and the test-authored dashboard and historical-review subprocesses.
conditions: The event loop has queued a callback before the wake-up send is attempted.
The selector can return from its configured wait and the loop thread can run.
exclusions: Product-owned loop construction and production server runtime.
Callbacks blocked by unrelated I/O, cancellation, or an executor job that does not finish.

evidence: BUG-R16 control and sandbox population in the round-1 freeze evidence

statement: The test-owned asyncio loops cap each idle selector wait at 50 milliseconds so they can process queued work and run normal executor shutdown when a socket wake-up is refused.
